page: Microsoft Azure E32ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Edsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and is equipped with a substantial 480 MB L3 cache. This instance is configured with 256.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. It includes 1890 GB of local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage configurations. No GPUs are bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data indicates balanced performance across compute and memory subsystems. The instance achieves average-tier results in stress-ng single-core (2238.28) and multi-core (34203.68) CPU tests. Memory bandwidth is measured at 146.04 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 62.52 GB/sec for write operations. Single-threaded gzip compression is a notable highlight, reaching top-tier performance at 36.05 GB/sec. For database workloads, the server handles 53.04 million Redis SET operations per second and scores 14087.31 in PassMark database operations, both falling within the average tier.

The hardware profile presents specific tradeoffs, particularly in artificial intelligence workloads. While prompt processing for a medium 7B LLM model is strong at 190.8 tokens/sec, text generation for a large 70B model is weak, yielding only 2.69 tokens/sec due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory density and large local storage capacity make it a resource-efficient choice for memory-intensive applications without the overhead of specialized GPU hardware. It is best suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data analytics, and enterprise applications requiring high memory-to-core ratios.
